nodes.label: Nav Services Dropdown Initiative
nodes.rationale: The global nav was cramped at 768-1100px viewport widths, the 'Music Guides' label could wrap to two lines, and the four commercial occasion pages (weddings/funerals/corporate/christmas) were reachable only via services.html, losing internal-link-equity distribution. Fixing cramping alone would leave those pages buried, and surfacing them as new top-level items would worsen cramping, so the two problems had to be solved together via CSS nowrap safety rules plus a Services dropdown.

nodes.label: Services Page Hub Redesign Initiative
nodes.rationale: services.html carried 102 inbound links while weddings.html had only 17 (per SEO audit finding), and the ~2,097-line page duplicated prose already present on the dedicated occasion pages. Redesigned into a lean ~500-600-word scannable hub (marquee-quote hero, 5-occasion list, 6-card ensemble grid) that pushes link weight to the commercial pillar pages, following on from the nav-dropdown work that first surfaced those pillar pages in the global nav.

nodes.label: Christmas Expansion & Seasonal SEO Initiative
nodes.rationale: Christmas is the highest-value season for a choir-for-hire business, but the site's entire Christmas surface was one corporate-only page (missing FAQ schema and absent from llms.txt) plus six guides, with zero Christmas content across all 52 area pages. Twelve net-net-new pages were added to own two distinct, non-cannibalising head-term families -- 'carol service' and 'hire carol singers' -- ahead of the September booking-research peak (the site's own copy says December dates fill by mid-September).

nodes.label: Competitive Capture Programme Initiative
nodes.rationale: To capture enquiries lost to The London Funeral Singers, LCS needed a sourced, verifiable comparison page built on three checkable differences: price (24-38% cheaper inc. VAT), repertoire allowance (up to three hymns vs their one performance piece), and how the ensemble is assembled (small hand-picked team under a named Artistic Director vs their 'over 150 auditioned singers' claim). Point 3 required repairing the site first -- removing false 'VAT-registered' claims from 6 B2B pages and a near-verbatim-competitor '150+ singers' claim from 13 places -- before the comparison's central claim could be made honestly. A new build-gated validator (validate_competitor_claims.py) and its test are the repo's first test, so a claims-integrity check couldn't silently pass vacuously.

nodes.label: Value, Bespoke Care & On-Page SEO Initiative
nodes.rationale: The site is SEO-mature (canonical/hreflang/OG, schema, sitemap, llms.txt all done); the next tier of improvement is conversion plus a short list of genuine on-page SEO gaps. With no usable GA4/Search Console/enquiry data, changes must be best-practice-driven rather than A/B-tested. The owner's thesis -- price value is real but buried in prose, and bespoke personal care is described in paragraphs but never dramatised -- is packaged as two reusable, site-wide components (a value block and a care strip) across all four service lines, deliberately avoiding a headcount ('150+ musicians') trust signal in favour of the Artistic Director's Oxford credential, consistent with the positioning correction made in the Competitive Capture programme.

nodes.label: SEO & Conversion Improvements Initiative
nodes.rationale: Competitor The London Funeral Singers used aggressive schema (AggregateRating, FAQPage), dense trust signals, and 22 targeted articles; LCS content converted poorly due to friction between reading and enquiring. Three workstreams (schema/technical SEO, content enrichment, conversion-path improvements) closed the gap across ~98 pages. Note: the AggregateRating/Review approach this plan propagated sitewide was later fully reversed by ROADMAP item R1, once self-serving review schema was identified as a Google policy violation.

nodes.label: Site Improvements Programme (v2)
nodes.rationale: A follow-up audit after the March SEO/conversion overhaul found one schema gap (christmas.html missing AggregateRating, added after the propagation commit) and one limitation (placeholder OG image). The reviewer's v2 revision deliberately dropped aesthetically risky speculative tasks (dark mode, share buttons, micro-interactions) to protect the funeral-service brand's reverent, still aesthetic, and reduced a 5-page hymn-page batch to 2 to protect content quality.

nodes.label: Music Guides Index Redesign Initiative
nodes.rationale: The /music-guides/ index had grown to 31+ dense, visually identical entries in a single ~2,600px-tall column with no filter, showing irrelevant content (e.g. funeral content to a wedding visitor) above the fold — emotionally jarring and commercially poor. Redesigned into a filterable card grid with category chips and a global nav dropdown, which first required extracting the site's nav/footer into shared partials (a one-time migration across 102 hand-authored HTML files) so the new markup only had to be written once.

nodes.label: SEO Audit Fixes Initiative
nodes.rationale: Addresses all 55 actionable findings across 13 themes from the 2026-05-08 SEO audit in a single comprehensive PR, executed as sequential phases (P1-P8) to avoid file-edit conflicts. Items requiring human/dashboard action (GBP claims, directory citations, GSC/GA4 credentials, Fastly VCL security headers) are diverted into a new top-level MANUAL-ACTIONS-REQUIRED.md rather than silently skipped, establishing that convention for later initiatives.
